## 13.0A Vulkan GPU Backend Override (v02.227) [TAI-VK-001]

Operator decision D7 (2026-10-31: "i want pure vulkan, no wgpu") and decision D1 (2026-10-30:
"Drop egui") apply to all of Section 13. The clauses in this sub-section override every
incompatible GPU-backend phrase, dependency pin, shader file name, code sample and test
instruction elsewhere in Section 13, in the same way [TAI-SDB-001] overrides legacy storage
wording. They do not change any CPU-f64 lane, quantity, pass order, tolerance or acceptance.

**[TAI-VK-002] GPU backend.** Every Tailor and BodyKit GPU lane (interactive XPBD, collision,
viewport, PBR, bake and toon passes) MUST run on Vulkan as a typed client of the centralized GPU
owner of section 15.5 ([GUI-DESKTOP-025], [GUI-DESKTOP-028]) and render through the Vulkan-backed
path of section 15.4. `wgpu`, WGSL, Naga, `wgsl_to_wgpu`, `egui`, `egui-wgpu` and `eframe` MUST NOT
be a dependency of any Tailor product crate (`tailor-solver`, `handshake_core::tailor`, the Tailor
viewport).

**[TAI-VK-003] Legacy notation and unnamed choices.** Code samples in this section still written in
WGSL syntax or against the wgpu API are legacy notation. Their binding numbers, struct fields and
field order, sizes, counts, pass order and dispatch rules remain normative; their WGSL syntax and
wgpu type, method and crate names do not authorize wgpu or WGSL. This specification names no
Vulkan binding crate, shader source language or shader build tool. Until it does, that gap MUST
NOT be read as permission to use wgpu or WGSL; the choices are open spec items recorded with the
v02.227 changelog entry.
